description:
Cross-platform encrypted email client

Aster Mail is a cross-platform, end-to-end encrypted email client built for Aster Privacy. Features quantum-safe encryption and zero-knowledge architecture.
Aster Mail
Note
These files are for new installations. If Aster Mail is already installed, it updates automatically.
What's new
- To see what a receipt or shipping card found in a message, click its info button. The form for reviewing a card is also more compact.
Fixed
- Sender names that use hidden characters or letters that look like Latin letters, and domains built to resemble a real one, now show a warning instead of passing as a trusted sender.
- Images in forwarded messages stay blocked until you choose to load them, the same as in the original message.
- Messages from another device that can't be authenticated are now marked as unverified, and an older copy of your encryption state can no longer replace a newer one.
- Receipt and shipping cards no longer appear on messages you sent.
- Very large messages open faster.
- Updates are now signed with a key used only for Aster Mail. Your installed app checks the new key automatically.
Verify the APK
Every Aster Mail APK in this release is signed with the Aster release certificate. Before you install one, check that its signing certificate matches this fingerprint.
- Package name: org.astermail.android
- SHA-256 certificate fingerprint: 88:B0:A8:A6:FB:94:EE:73:A4:54:A0:F9:27:32:BD:40:8E:92:E5:1E:C1:E9:55:67:44:E5:F0:05:56:10:09:77
To check a downloaded APK on a computer, run apksigner verify --print-certs Aster-Mail.apk from the Android SDK build tools. The certificate SHA-256 digest line shows the same value in lowercase without colons. To check the app on your phone, use a verification app such as AppVerifier.
If you install Aster Mail from Google Play, Google Play signs it with its own key, so that copy has a different fingerprint: C2:0D:A2:1D:DA:9D:35:45:26:75:34:19:11:B0:01:E5:32:80:B5:C8:91:AB:90:9B:13:BF:27:63:77:40:A6:AF
